title: Column gravity anchors and density transitions for hybrid virtual tables
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Goal: Introduce a lightweight interaction pattern we’re calling "column gravity anchors" plus a density transition system for hybrid virtualized tables (row-virtualized lists that also support tile-like compact cells). This is intended to make column resizing and density changes feel predictable during jittery scroll/virtualization boundaries and to reduce accidental layout shifts when users switch density or reorder columns.

Scope: design tokens mapping for density ramps, micro-animation guidance for transitions (duration, easing, opacity masks), keyboard affordances for gravity-anchor toggles, and a migration plan for legacy table tokens. Work includes low-fi and hi-fi prototypes, accessibility checklist, and an engineering spec for telemetry events and performance budgets (60fps target for transitions on typical dedicated dev machines).

Why: Current resize and density mode behavior in heavy virtualized tables can cause perceived layout jumps and loss of focus. Many support tickets cite cursor drift during column drags and confusing collapse thresholds when switching density. Column gravity anchors aim to give the UI a small set of deterministic snap anchors (not hard snapping) that reduce micro-shifts while preserving fluidity.

Out of scope: full rewrite of virtualization runtime; changes to backend pagination or data models. We will coordinate with ENG for kernel-level perf if required but remain interface-first for initial rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens: density-compact, density-default, density-spacious mapped to padding/typography/token values and documented in token catalog
Prototype: Figma interactive showing column gravity anchors during drag + density toggle with animation curves and masks
Accessibility: keyboard-only column grab + gravity-anchor toggle works; screen reader announcements for density change and anchor activation
Perf: CSS/Render approach runs at >=60fps on target test machine (documented in PR checklist) or provides fallback to reduced animation when budget exceeded
Engineered: ENG has a minimal implementation plan with telemetry events defined (density_change, gravity_anchor_engaged, column_resize_start/complete) and a rollout strategy to 10% canary
Migration: migration notes for any breaking token name changes and a codemod-ish suggestion for teams using legacy tokens
comments: 2025-01-20 10:12 — Amina Patel: Initial proposal written after reviewing support trends and recent design audits. Attached early sketches and a short Loom capturing the problem on large, mixed-content tables.

2025-01-23 14:05 — Linh Tran: Ran quick hallway usability with three PMs; consistent pain point when density toggles during long scrolls. They preferred a subtle anchor over full snap. Added keyboard requirement: Ctrl+Enter to toggle gravity anchor mode for power users.

2025-01-29 09:41 — Diego Morales (Eng): Reviewed concept. Concern about virtualization layer exposing enough layout hints to place anchors without forcing full remeasure. Suggest API: expose per-column preferred anchor offsets + optional stable-anchor flag. ENG will prototype a cheap heuristic first.

2025-02-03 16:22 — Accessibility review (R. Kim): Confirmed screen reader requirements. Recommend 1) announce "density: compact" on toggle, 2) announce "column anchor engaged" when users lock an anchor via keyboard. Add focus management checklist for column resize flow.

2025-02-05 11:18 — Design critique: team liked masking/alpha fade as an approach to hide micro-shifts. Concern about too many knobs for users; plan to keep default automatic, advanced toggle in table settings.

2025-02-07 08:03 — Linh Tran: Updated Figma prototype link and added animation specs. Ready for ENG spike. Next: sync with ENG on telemetry naming and minimal DOM/CSS approach (prefer transform-based animations).
notes: Rollout plan: 1) ENG spike to test anchor heuristic, 2) small canary behind feature flag, 3) collect telemetry for 2 weeks, 4) iterate on animation curves. Telemetry schema and naming to be added to ENG spike ticket. If perf budget fails, fallback will be instantaneous layout (no animation) and a follow-up opt-in animation release.
